topic: Analytics discrepancies in mall session data
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on discrepancies found when comparing staging and production analytics for mall sessions, specifically regarding dwell time and total traffic. Initial review revealed that the reported dwell time changes were likely due to incorrect headers in the displayed table.

Regarding total traffic, it was noted that simply increasing session duration (dwell time) should not proportionally increase total traffic or unique user counts. The discrepancy was attributed to how sessions are counted: on production, multiple screen visits from a single user over a period are merged into one session, while staging might be counting individual, shorter segments.

It was decided that the reporting needs improvement to better reflect user behavior by adding metrics for frequency per mall and frequency per screen. The team agreed that traffic per screen should also be considered.
decisions: The current dwell time discrepancies are likely due to incorrect table headers.
New analytics metrics should include frequency per mall, frequency per screen, and potentially traffic per screen.
action_items: Define the scope of new reporting metrics (frequency/traffic per screen) during a management meeting on Monday.
